claim: A 20 in box fan develops only about 27 to 55 Pa at shut-off
law: Quadratic fan curve fitted to Dal Porto et al. 2022 (12 % flow loss at 6.2 Pa, low speed); fan laws (pressure scales with speed squared) with the 1.42 high-to-low CADR ratio as the speed ratio (A2)
check: 27.5 Pa at low speed, about 55 Pa at high speed; a quadratic curve has no stall dip, so flows near shut-off are optimistic (independent review 2026-11-12: S1 weak, low-speed point applied to high-speed flows; fixed by carrying both)

claim: Four panels (0.98 m2 of face) let a box fan deliver 712 to 2277 m3/h (model, clean) at 9 to 34 Pa and 0.20 to 0.65 m/s face velocity
law: Fan curve against linear media resistance (Parker 38.2, Global Industrial 62.1 Pa per m/s; A3); UC Davis measured 443 to 500 cfm (753 to 850 m3/h) through a four-filter cube
check: The measured airflow sits at the model's low end; linear extrapolation overstates media resistance at low velocity (UC Davis estimate 5 to 7.5 Pa against 9 to 15 Pa modelled) and the upper end exceeds every measurement (independent review 2026-11-12). Design figures use measured CADR (S3), the model only brackets

claim: One four-panel cube on high gives a clean air delivery rate of about 398 to 459 m3/h
law: Four-panel CR boxes: EPA ORD MS2 virus aerosol CADR 234 cfm (398 m3/h); UC Davis 239 to 270 cfm (406 to 459 m3/h, from a 54 % efficiency rating); Dal Porto et al. 2022 five-panel cube 1,020 to 1,450 m3/h as a reference only
check: PR-001 targets at least 400 m3/h, which the lowest four-panel measurement (398) just misses; no measured size-resolved 0.3 to 3 um CADR exists for a four-panel cube, so V2 is the gate (independent review 2026-11-12: S3 weak, five-panel data removed from the CA2 range)

claim: MERV-13 media keeps about 40 to 50 % single-pass efficiency for 0.3 to 1 um at the cube's low face velocity
law: ASHRAE 52.2 MERV-13 minimums E1 50 %, E2 85 %, E3 90 % (NAFA guide); in use Dal Porto et al. 2022 found an effective 41 to 58 % and EPA's CADR of 234 cfm on 560 to 605 cfm implies 39 to 42 %
check: Face velocity 0.20 to 0.65 m/s, below the 1.5 to 2.5 m/s at which panels are rated; humidity can discharge electret media; in-situ efficiency is measured, not assumed

claim: In a 50 m2 x 3 m ward (150 m3) one cube gives 2.7 to 3.1 eACH, so CDC's 5 ACH needs 2 cubes and Lancet 'better' 6 ACHe 2 to 3
law: eACH = CADR / room volume (well mixed); CDC aim for 5 ACH of clean air, adding ventilation and filtration; Lancet Commission NADR good 4, better 6 ACHe
check: 750 m3/h for 5 ACH; two cubes give 795 to 917 m3/h (5.3 to 6.1 eACH) clean; existing ventilation adds to it (independent review 2026-11-12: corrected from 1 to 2 cubes)

claim: In a 20 m2 x 3 m clinic room (60 m3) one clean cube on high gives 6.6 to 7.6 eACH, above CDC 5 ACH and Lancet 6 ACHe
law: eACH = CADR / room volume
check: 300 m3/h for 5 ACH; 360 m3/h for 6. On low speed (UC Davis 163 to 165 cfm) 4.6 eACH, and with loaded panels 5 ACH is not assured, so the change point is set by PR-021 (independent review 2026-11-12)

claim: A 1 mm gap at the deck gasket, the four corner seams and the tray seam lets less than 10 % of the air bypass the media
law: Orifice leak Q = 0.6 A sqrt(2 dP / rho) in parallel with the media; 6.2 m of seam; worst case over both fans, both shut-off pressures and both media
closed_by: CAR-CAL-001 section 7 (best case 3.7 %; 2 mm worst 15 %); smoke-pencil check at TRL 4; independent review 2026-11-12 added the tray seam

claim: Loaded panels cut the airflow to 467 to 1509 m3/h at 2.6 times initial resistance, and to 204 to 667 m3/h at 7.3 times
law: Parker final resistance 1.0 in w.g. against 0.39 initial; UL Chemical Insights dust-loaded filters 2.0 in w.g. against 0.274 clean
check: The fan's low pressure makes the cube sensitive to loading; a change interval is set from a loaded-flow test, not assumed (A7)

claim: The added filter load does not raise motor current, and winding temperature stays below the insulation rating
law: UL Chemical Insights report 200 (2021): five box fans, 0.4 to 0.9 A, 52.8 to 97.8 W, current unaffected by filter condition; highest winding 92 C against 105 C (Class A); no ignition in 7 h blocked
check: Listing standards set measured limits below the 105 C class rating, so 92 C may sit near a limit; the tests had the fan upright, the cube lays it flat (S25). Use only fans listed to UL 507 or IEC 60335-2-80 with thermal protection; check per model (V5; independent review 2026-11-12)

claim: The kit adds no electrical part; the fan's own listing (UL 507 or IEC 60335-2-80) carries the electrical safety case
law: UL 507 (electric fans); IEC 60335-2-80:2024 (fans)
check: Whether a listing still covers a fan run with filters strapped to it is to assess with a listing body; the UL report found no hazard in 7 h fully blocked

claim: The cube emits no ozone: it has no UV lamp, ioniser or electrostatic stage
law: Ozone forms from oxygen below about 240 nm (Luminus note) or in corona discharge; UL 2998 benchmark under 0.005 ppm; CARB limit 0.050 ppm (UL 867 method)
check: Mechanical filtration only; UL 2998 is a benchmark to cite, not a pass, until tested

claim: Filtration lowers the airborne particle concentration that carries respiratory viruses; it does not by itself prevent infection, so only CADR is claimed
law: EPA ORD chamber test: CR boxes cut airborne MS2 by 97 % in 30 min and 99.4 % in 60 min in 3,000 ft3; CDC presents ACH as one layer of risk reduction, a goal not a hard rule
check: Claims limited to particle CADR and eACH (CAR-CLM-001); no infection outcome is claimed

claim: The cube with its fan (7.7 kg) stands on a 10 deg incline and needs about 27 N at the top to tip
law: Tipping about the feet: tan(angle) = half base / centre of gravity height; 10 deg incline as in household appliance stability tests (IEC 60335-1 clause 20.1, to confirm against the current edition)
check: Tip angle 28 deg against 10; 27 N is a bump, not a lean, so it stands on the floor, never on a table, away from walkways or tied to a fixed object (PR-012)

claim: The cube with its fan weighs under 10 kg, a one-person carry
law: Model volumes x densities; panels 0.68 kg (A11); twin-wall sheet 0.75 kg/m2 (A10); fan 7.25 lb (listing)

claim: The assembled cube passes a 700 mm door and the kit packs flat
law: Model envelope; two 610 x 914 mm sheets and four 44 mm panels
closed_by: CAR-CAL-001 section 9 (640 mm tall; flat pack about 0.05 m3)

claim: The cube is combustible (card frames, synthetic media, PP sheet) but adds no ignition source; fire behaviour is to rate
law: UL Chemical Insights report 200: no ignition with clean, smoke- or dust-loaded filters, motor housing 54 C at most; polypropylene burns
check: Panels with a UL 900 classification from the supplier and flame-retardant sheet are asked for; keep 1 m from heaters and flames

claim: First assembly takes under 15 minutes (estimate 8 to 12 min)
law: Step count from the build plan: tray, four panels, four angles, two straps, deck, gasket, fan, two straps (A12)
check: No tape, no tools; to time with the personas at TRL 4 (V6)

claim: A filter change takes under 2 minutes (the deck's cassette-swap target)
law: Step count (A12): release four straps, lift the fan and deck, swap four panels, refit
check: Whole set 4 to 6 min; one panel 1.5 to 2.5 min. Not met on paper for the whole set; changing the target to read per panel changes a user-facing requirement, so it goes to Amish

claim: A four-panel cube on a box fan gives about 4 m3/h of clean air per watt; a five-panel cube on a stronger fan about 15
law: UC Davis four-filter: 239 to 270 cfm CADR on 102 to 103 W; EPA 234 cfm; Dal Porto five-panel 8.7 to 8.9 cfm per W; running 24 h a day 587 to 858 kWh a year
check: 3.9 to 14.8 m3/h per W (independent review 2026-11-12: the earlier 15 m3/h per W was refuted for four panels and corrected)

claim: Kit parts cost no more than the USD 150 value-engineering target
law: Priced BOM (bom/bom.csv), cited prices checked 2026-11-12; the fan is excluded (the facility's own; a new box fan adds USD 23.49); filters recur at USD 54 a set (CAR-MKT-001)

claim: The PP tray, deck and angles wipe clean with 70 % alcohol or 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite; the panels are replaced, not wiped
law: Polypropylene resists dilute hypochlorite and alcohols (supplier chemical-resistance tables, to confirm for the bought sheet); pleated media and card are not cleanable
check: Panels are consumables; wiping only the sheet parts; disinfectant contact time per the facility's IPC procedure

claim: Card frames hold their shape in a humid field site
law: Card loses stiffness when damp; synthetic media does not absorb water
check: Corner angles and straps carry the panels; at high humidity check sag at each change; a moisture-resistant frame is asked of the supplier

claim: The fan's own guards stay in place; the kit adds no pinch point at the blades
law: Box fans have guards both sides; the deck and straps sit outside them
check: The two hold-down straps now cross the solid fan frame at 261 mm from the centre, outside the 484 mm guard, so strap tension cannot push the guard into the blades (independent review 2026-11-12, fixed F3)

claim: CADR and eACH are first-order estimates; the fan-curve uncertainty on one box fan (rating against measurement) is a factor of about 3
law: Rated 1,800 cfm against 568 cfm derived from a measured cube
check: Every flow is shown as a range with both fans and both media resistances; a unit is accepted only on a measured CADR

claim: A box fan may run lying flat, blowing up
law: Neither the UL report nor a fan listing covers this orientation (bearing load, motor cooling, controls on top)
check: Most published CR boxes run this way; ask the fan maker and test motor temperature flat (V5)

claim: On low speed, for quiet, a four-panel cube gives about 280 m3/h
law: UC Davis four-filter cube speed 1: 163 to 165 cfm CADR, 70 to 71 W; noise not measured in the sources
check: Clinic room 4.6 eACH on low; noise in dBA at 1 m to measure (V8, PR-018)

claim: eACH figures assume the room air is well mixed
law: CADR / V is a well-mixed estimate; short-circuit from the outlet back to the inlets lowers it
check: Place the cube with the outlet jet free and the inlet sides 300 mm clear; mixing to check in a room test (V3)

claim: Two cubes meet the Lancet 'good' 10 L/s per person for up to about 22 ward occupants
law: Lancet Commission NADR good 10 L/s (36 m3/h) per person, better 14 L/s
check: 795 m3/h / 36 m3/h per person; with more occupants the per-person criterion governs and a third cube is planned

claim: Used panels hold captured particles and are bagged and disposed of as the facility's waste rules require
law: Captured particles stay on the media; handling a loaded filter can release dust
check: Change with gloves, bag at the cube, follow the facility's IPC procedure; disposal route to agree with the partner (UR-005)

claim: Fans sold for 230 V, 50 Hz at field sites have different curves from the 120 V data
law: All cited measurements used 120 V US box fans
check: Use the local listed fan and measure its CADR in the cube (V2)

claim: The cube's eACH adds to the room's ventilation; it does not replace it
law: CDC: ACH and eACH from filtration can be added for comparison with the 5 ACH goal
check: Stated in the claims and on the label

claim: The fan frame seals to the deck on the foam square
law: Gasket 510 mm square lies inside the 521 x 552 mm fan frame and outside the 480 mm opening
check: Leak counted in S7; the frame's own corner gaps outside the blades to check
